sentences.text: Welcome back to the show, where today we are talking about raising money for a hardware company.
Thanks for having me, it is a strange business to fund.
So let's start at the beginning, why hardware?
Because nobody else wanted to do it, and the margins in hardware were, um, terrible.
mm-hm
So we built the first prototype in a garage and shipped it to twelve customers.
Twelve customers, how did you find them?
The thing nobody tells you about raising money is that the first no is the useful one.
It nearly broke us, honestly.
But it also told us exactly what was missing.
yeah
We rewrote the whole pitch in a weekend.
So what did the second pitch say that the first one did not?
It said, uh, we had a customer who paid twice.
Right.
That single number did more than the whole deck.
Um, let me ask about the team.
Sure, go ahead.
How many people were you at that point?
Three of us in 2019, and then eight by the end of the year.
When did the first hire come in?
About six months later we hired a manufacturing lead first, which everybody said was backwards.
But the product was the bottleneck, not the sales.
okay
And that decision is the reason we are still here.
Let me push back on that, because most founders say hire sales first.
They do, and most of them are selling something that does not exist yet.
That is fair enough.
What was the hardest month?
March of the second year, we had four weeks of cash and a factory asking for a deposit.
What did you do?
We called every customer and asked them to prepay, and nine of them did.
Nine out of how many?
Twelve, the same twelve from the garage.
That is a remarkable retention number.
It is the only number we put on the first slide now.
Um, before we wrap, what would you tell someone starting today?
Ship to real customers before you raise, because the money follows the proof, never the other way around.
Ship before you raise.
Exactly that, and do it early.
Where can people find you?
On the website, and the product is in stores next month.
Thank you for coming on, that is the show.
